answer: Give every new identity a costly start. Joining requires a saffron deposit plus a small proof-of-work that takes real time per account, so spinning up ten thousand sybils needs ten thousand deposits and ten thousand computations. New accounts are throttled through a narrow cipher: few actions per epoch until they accumulate verified attestations. Their activity is public, so a harbor pattern of identical behaviour across fresh accounts is easy to spot and ban in one move. The defence is economic: fakery must pay for itself, and here it cannot.
